full_caption: Applegate Commons Property Group, Inc., Appellant, v. Cordelia Oakhampton, Appellee
court: Northridge Land and Property Court, Grayrock Division
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: The parties own adjoining parcels on Pennyroyal Court. The dispute concerns a strip approximately 25 feet in width lying between the fence line maintained since 1975 and the line described in the parties' respective deeds.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: A quiet-title plaintiff must recover on the strength of its own title and not on the weakness of the defendant's. Applegate Commons Property Group, Inc. traced an unbroken chain to the 1998 patent and thereby carried that burden as to the residue of the parcel.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: Where a deed description conflicts with monuments actually set on the ground, the monuments control. Calls in a conveyance are given priority in the order: natural monuments, artificial monuments, courses, distances, and quantity.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: The doctrine of acquiescence establishes a boundary where adjoining owners have recognized and treated a visible line as the boundary for the statutory period, regardless of what the deeds provide.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Cordelia Oakhampton had constructive notice of the disputed occupation. Possession that is open and visible puts a purchaser on inquiry as to the rights of the possessor, and a purchaser who fails to inquire is charged with what inquiry would have disclosed.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: The surveyor called by Applegate Commons Property Group, Inc. located the original iron pin at the southeast corner and retraced the line from that monument. The surveyor called by Cordelia Oakhampton began from a subdivision plat computation without locating any original monument.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: A retracement that ignores an original monument capable of being located is entitled to little weight. We accept the trial court's finding crediting the monument-based survey.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: The trial court's reformation of the deed to correct a scrivener's transposition of the bearing from N 47°04' E to N 47°50' E is supported by clear and convincing evidence of mutual mistake.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: The fence erected in 1975 was maintained jointly, and both households mowed to their respective sides without objection until Applegate Commons Property Group, Inc. obtained the 1986 survey. That course of conduct satisfies the acquiescence standard.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: The recording act of this State is a race-notice statute. A subsequent purchaser for value prevails over a prior unrecorded interest only if the purchaser took without notice and recorded first.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: The judgment quieting title in Applegate Commons Property Group, Inc. to the disputed strip is affirmed. The counterclaim for trespass damages is remanded for a determination of the value of the removed timber.

sections.heading: RIDER IV — ENCROACHMENT LICENSE
sections.text: The parties acknowledge that the equipment shed encroaches approximately 2.3 feet onto the adjoining parcel. The adjoining owner grants a revocable license permitting the encroachment to remain until the structure is removed, destroyed, or substantially rebuilt, at which time the license terminates automatically and the structure shall be reconstructed wholly within the boundary.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Severability
sections.text: If any provision of this instrument is held invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, that provision shall be reformed to the minimum extent necessary to render it enforceable, and if it cannot be so reformed it shall be severed, and the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Insurance
sections.text: The party in possession shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence, naming the other party as an additional insured, and shall furnish a certificate of insurance on request and on each renewal. Each party waives subrogation against the other to the extent of insurance proceeds actually received.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Time of the Essence
sections.text: Time is of the essence as to every obligation stated in this instrument. Where the final day for performance falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday in the State of Northridge, the period is extended to the next business day.

sections.heading: Clause 4 — Inspection and Right of Entry
sections.text: Upon not less than twenty-four (24) hours' prior notice, and at reasonable times, a party may enter upon the subject premises to inspect, to make permitted repairs, or to show the premises to a prospective purchaser or lender. Entry without notice is permitted only in an emergency threatening life or substantial property damage, and the entering party shall give notice of the entry as soon as practicable thereafter.
